Non-emergent: local rules plus initial conditions let you deduce the "expected" high-level pattern. Weakly emergent: they let you deduce an "unexpected" one by computation. | [LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) v3 | Greater than the parts: a review of the information decomposition approach to causal emergence | Mediano et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2111.06518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06518). A review, with no new theorem, of the ΦID theory of causal emergence. A supervenient feature V_t is k-th-order causally emergent iff Un⁽ᵏ⁾(V_t; X_t′ \| X_t) > 0. A system hosts such features iff Syn⁽ᵏ⁾(X_t; X_t′) > 0 (cited as Rosas et al. 2020, Theorem 1), and Syn⁽ᵏ⁾ = D⁽ᵏ⁾ + G⁽ᵏ⁾ (downward causation plus causal decoupling). The review's own additions are interpretive: the formalism is neutral between Granger and Pearl, coordinate dependence is defended as a feature, and it rebuts the charge that the theory makes no macro-versus-micro comparison. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-010); a short, accurate map of the ΦID emergence formalism and the right entry point to Rosas et al. 2020, which a reader will still need for the proofs, the assumptions and the redundancy-free practical criteria. | [LIT-027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md) v3 | Emergence as the conversion of information: a unifying theory | Varley et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2104.13368](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13368). Varley and Hoel apply a PID, with the Williams–Beer I_min redundancy, to past→future mutual information and summarise it with a new layer-weighted "synergy bias" B_syn ∈ [0,1]. Coarse-graining can raise B_syn at the macroscale. A macroscale XOR reaches 0.833, against 0.52 for its NAND/AND/OR implementation. In 200 random 3-node "Gaussian" TPMs expanded into equivalence-class micro/mesoscales with *identical* MI, every macroscale had higher B_syn, by ≈ 0.01–0.07 (r = 0.819 against macroscale B_syn). In 185 near-deterministic systems the change was mostly negative, down to ≈ −0.1. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-020); a clear, small-scale demonstration that coarse-graining can change the redundant/synergistic composition of information and not just its amount. | [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md) v3 | The Open Systems View | Cuffaro et al. (2021), [ARXIV-2112.11095](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11095). The paper argues philosophically, not formally, that the quantum theory of open systems "GT" is more fundamental than standard closed-system quantum theory "ST". GT treats states as density operators that evolve, in general, non-unitarily, and it admits not-completely-positive maps. The ontic and epistemic cases each win only on a second, interpretation- or practice-laden criterion: OntFund-2 and EpFund-2. On the first, formal criteria (OntFund-1, EpFund-1) the two frameworks tie, and the authors say so because Stinespring dilation and dropping the Lindblad terms translate in both directions (§4.1, §4.2.1). Explanatory fundamentality is granted only deflationarily (ExFund-1), and the authors recommend dropping the notion (§4.2.2). The step from there to "the open systems view is fundamental tout court" (§4.3) rests on the special sciences and on "there are no other options". | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-077); worth reading as the clearest statement of the "open systems view" and of the distinction between a view, a framework, a theory and a model (§2, §4.1, §5.2). Read it knowing that its fundamentality verdict is carried by interpretive premises (OntFund-2, EpFund-2) and a deflationary step, not by any formal asymmetry between the frameworks. |
| [LIT-045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md) v3 | Structural Realism | Ladyman (2007), <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/structural-realism/>. The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the pessimistic meta-induction: what survives theory change, and what we are entitled to believe, is a theory's mathematical or relational structure. It then separates an epistemic version (we can know only structure) from an ontic version (structure is all there is). The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the lesson of theory change. What is retained, and what we are entitled to believe, is structure, understood by ontic structuralists as modal structure. It sorts the view into an epistemic form, which falls to the Newman/Demopoulos–Friedman triviality result when stated as a Ramsey sentence (§3.2), and an ontic form with seven distinguishable theses, from eliminativism about individuals to "objects are constructs" (§4). The ontic form is motivated by quantum non-individuality and entanglement, gauge symmetry and the hole argument. The entry closes with seven objections, each answered in the author's own voice (§5). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md)); the standard map of the structural-realism literature, written by the founder of OSR. Read §2 for the theory-change argument, §3.2 for the Newman problem and §4's seven OSR theses. Treat §5's rebuttals as the author's position, not as the field's settled view. |
| [LIT-062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md) v3 | On the reality of the quantum state | Pusey et al. (2011), [ARXIV-1111.3328](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3328). Take pure states \|ψ0⟩, \|ψ1⟩ with \|⟨ψ0\|ψ1⟩\| = cos θ. Assume (a) a model assigns each preparation a distribution µ_i(λ) over physical states, (b) n independent preparations yield the product distribution µ_{x1}(λ1)⋯µ_{xn}(λn), and (c) outcome probabilities depend only on (λ1, …, λn). If the model's predictions are within ε of quantum theory, then D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} for any n with 2^{1/n} − 1 ≤ tan(θ/2) (Eq. 7, App. B). At ε = 0 the distributions for distinct pure states cannot overlap on a set of non-zero measure, so Harrigan–Spekkens ψ-epistemic models are ruled out. | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-030); the founding ψ-ontology theorem. It is short, fully proved (App. A–B), and still the reference that every later ψ-epistemic/ψ-ontic argument, including LIT-007 §I.C and LIT-090, positions itself against. Read it with its assumption (b)–(c) in view, since that is where every response pushes. |
| [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md) v3 | Could wavefunctions simultaneously represent knowledge and reality? | Hance et al. (2021), [ARXIV-2101.06436](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.06436). The paper argues, informally and without formal results, that Harrigan–Spekkens' ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic are contradictories only by stipulation. On the informal senses, "represents reality" and "represents knowledge", a wavefunction can be both. It offers a weaker sufficient condition for "epistemic" (Eq. 6: for some ψ, A, S, the response function A(S\|λ) is not equal to the Born probability p^ψ_A(S) throughout Λψ), which non-overlapping models can meet. It concludes that PBR "shows that wavefunctions cannot overlap on state space, but it says nothing about whether they are epistemic in the broader sense", so it "does not rule out all epistemic models" (§V). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-072); a short, clear statement that ψ-epistemic in the Harrigan–Spekkens sense is narrower than "epistemic", worth reading for §III–V as a terminological caution when citing PBR. | [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md) | What Is It Like to Be a Bat? | Nagel (1974), [DOI-10.2307/2183914](https://doi.org/10.2307/2183914). An organism has conscious states if and only if there is something it is like to be that organism. That subjective character belongs to a type of point of view, and it is left out by every functional, intentional or causal analysis, since each is compatible with its absence. Reduction elsewhere moves away from a point of view toward the objective; here that move leads away from the thing being explained. So physicalism may be true, but we have no conception of how it could be. Nagel proposes an "objective phenomenology" that would describe experience to beings who cannot have it. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-089); the source of the "something it is like" criterion of consciousness that the record's AI-consciousness work (LIT-056) adopts as its target, and of the argument that no functional analysis can settle whether that criterion is met. |
